```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
Cp <- sample(seq(1.2,2.0,0.1),1)
Cpk <- round(Cp - sample(seq(0.2,0.6,0.1),1),1)
```
Question
========

A process has $C_p=`r Cp`$ and $C_{pk}=`r Cpk`$.

Which conclusion is most appropriate?

Answerlist
----------

* The process spread is adequate, but the process is not perfectly centered.
* The process is perfectly centered between specifications.
* The process is out of statistical control.
* The specification limits are wider than the process spread because $C_{pk}>C_p$.

Solution
========

When $C_{pk}<C_p$, the process has potential capability but is shifted away from the target or center.
